text:
mira: Heads-up — bringing up a new Mistral-derived variant (borealis-7b) for Dedicated. Smoke results show weird repetition / turn-taking after ~2k tokens in summarization runs. Suspect rotary phase / tokenizer interaction.
sam: Can you share a short failing transcript + config?
mira: Pasting minimal repro and notes below. Only happens when convert -> int4 (our usual quant pipeline). FP16 baseline is fine.
----
mira: Repro steps:
1) convert model with rpe->rotary conversion patch we use
2) quantize to int4 (groupwise) using quantize_v2.py
3) run summarize-long-context eval (open source prompt set)
Command: `python run_eval.py --model /tmp/borealis/converted --batch 1 --max_tokens 4096 --task summarization`
Observed: coherent until ~1800 tokens, then repeated clause "the report indicates" starts appearing every 30-60 tokens. Deterministic with seed.
Logs: `token_id window around repetition shows jump at token 2047 -> 2050`
----
devon: Interesting. Two hypotheses: 1) rotary scaling/stride mismatch during conversion causes KV cache misalignment at wrap boundary; 2) tokenizer normalizer (we apply NFKC) maps soft-hyphen/zwj differently vs upstream causing off-by-one token insert.
zara: Any differences in embedding matrix ordering vs Gemma/Qwen conversions? We had a similar pattern with Gemma-lite when a proj-order mismatch caused phase resonance.
mira: Embedding checksums match upstream, but kvcache index test shows a head-wise offset on half of heads. So not global ordering.
sam: Can you dump a head-wise rotary phase matrix for step where repetition starts? Small script: 
```
# dump head rotary check
python tools/rotary_check.py --model /tmp/borealis/converted --layer 11 --head 3 --out head11_h3.npy
```
If head-level phase wraps at different token index than others, that points to per-head headmap mismatch.
ci-bot: conversion-job-452: failed at quant step (non-fatal), artifact saved /artifacts/452/conv-log.txt
devon: On tokenizer: try running the same prompt with our NFLEX normalizer (no NFKC) and compare token sequences. If sequences diverge only around soft-hyphen or emoji clusters, that could be the trigger.
mira: Ran that — NFLEX vs NFKC differ around ZWJ+emoji and hyphenation points. Repro shows repetition only with NFKC-normalized tokens.
zara: So two interacting bugs: tokenization injects an extra zero-width token at boundary and conversion produced a per-head kv offset that becomes visible when cache wraps at that token index. Combo explains deterministic repetition at ~2048.
sam: Nice triage. For short-term mitigation: 1) force tokenization to NFLEX for Dedicated onboard, 2) pin rotary scaling to 0.98 in conversion (we've seen that smooths head drift), 3) add KV cache alignment assert in runtime.
mira: Agreed. I ran a quick patch: `--rotary-scale 0.98` + NFLEX normalizer; summarization run now goes to 4096 with no repetition in 10/10 runs. Token-level perf same within noise.
devon: We should add a unit-test: feed a synthetic sequence that triggers wrap (length = model.max_position + 5) and assert kvcache indices are monotonic across heads. Also add a tokenizer regression test comparing byte-level offsets across normalizers.
zara: Also report to model-conversion upstream (borealis repo) — the original conversion script assumes global head ordering which isn't true for this fork. Could be a generator mismatch during export.
mira: Filing follow-ups:
- mira: onboard patch (NFLEX + rotary=0.98) -> PR against dedicated-configs (owner mira)
- devon: add kvcache alignment unit tests (owner devon)
- sam: open issue on conversion tool w/ head-level ordering assumption and link artifact (owner sam)
- zara: prepare a short eval blurb for console explaining mitigation and quality delta (owner zara)
Anyone object to shipping the mitigation to Dedicated as a hotfix?
sam: +1 from me, label it hotfix.
devon: +1. We should schedule a follow release for the conversion tool update.
ci-bot: deploy-job-301: staged patch mira/dedicated-hotfix deployed to canary (10% traffic). Monitoring for repetition regressions for 2h.
mira: I'll watch the canary. If no regressions, promote. Thanks y'all.
----
Notes for postmortem: not a single-source bug — tokenizer normalization + conversion head-order assumption + int4 quantization combined to surface the repetition regression. We avoided customer impact by quick NFLEX rollback + slight rotary re-scale.
